angles.name: Devotional
angles.blurb: A short reflection that moves from the text to the heart.
outline: Open with a moment from ordinary life that the passage speaks to
Read the passage slowly, one phrase at a time
Name what it reveals about God
Name what it asks of us
Close with a one-sentence prayer
titles: What {theme} Looks Like on a Tuesday

angles.name: Bible study
angles.blurb: Work through the passage verse by verse and draw the point out.
outline: Set the scene: who is speaking, and to whom?
Walk through the passage in short sections
Note repeated words and the turning point
State the main idea in one sentence
Apply it to one concrete decision this week
titles: Three Things You May Have Missed in {ref}

angles.name: Personal story
angles.blurb: Tell a true story and let the passage interpret it.
outline: Start in the middle of the story, not the beginning
Describe what you expected and what actually happened
Show where the passage met you in it
Say plainly what changed
Invite the reader into the same hope
titles: I Did Not Expect {ref} to Change My Week

angles.name: Practical list
angles.blurb: Give the reader something they can use today.
outline: Promise a specific, modest outcome in the title
Anchor every point in the passage
Keep each point to one sentence plus one example
End with the one thing to do first
titles: What {ref} Teaches Us About {theme} in 60 Seconds

angles.name: Honest questions
angles.blurb: Take the hardest objection seriously and answer it gently.
outline: State the objection in its strongest form
Acknowledge what is right about it
Bring the passage to bear, not just your opinion
Say what remains a mystery
Close with what you would say to a friend over coffee

angles.name: Two passages
angles.blurb: Set two passages side by side and let them illuminate each other.
outline: Introduce both passages and why you paired them
Show where they agree
Show where the tension is
Resolve it, or say why it stays open
Land on what both passages ask of you
titles: What the Bible Says Twice About {theme}

angles.name: Church season
angles.blurb: Tie the passage to where the church is in the year.
outline: Name the season and what it is for
Read the passage in that light
Show what the season is training us to see
Suggest one practice for the weeks ahead

opening: Open with a scene your reader has lived.
Start with a question you could not answer.
Begin with the sentence you did not want to read.
Start small: one detail, one moment, one room.
Begin with the prayer you were afraid to pray.
